title: Expressing one quantity as a percentage of another
summary: Express a part or comparison quantity as a percentage of a clearly identified reference quantity, including quantities given in different units.
objectives: Identify the quantity that represents the whole or reference value.
Convert compared quantities to the same unit before calculating a percentage.
Use part divided by whole, multiplied by 100%, and check whether the result is reasonable.

sections.title: A percentage compares with a reference quantity

blocks.text: A percentage answers ‘how many hundredths of the reference quantity?’ First identify the part and the whole or reference. Then use
. The denominator is the quantity being compared against, so choosing it correctly matters.

The fraction must compare like units. Convert lengths, masses, times or money to the same unit before dividing. A useful estimate should come first: a part smaller than the reference gives less than 100%, while an equal quantity gives 100%.

sections.title: Worked example: convert units before comparing

prompt.text: Express 36 cm as a percentage of 1.2 m.

sections.verification_note: Comparing 36 with 1.2 without converting would give 3000%, which cannot be right for a part smaller than the whole.

feedback.text: Calculate 24 divided by 80, then multiply by 100%. The result is 30%.
